# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🤙]

The broadcast name was wrong — a speak with no recipient named reaches everyone able to hear it, so I drop the `to` field entirely and keep the message whole for both, with the sign-code gesture still aimed at Mute alone.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking — you can both hear me. Everything I see on the bomb: the display shows zero. The light is green. There are exactly three wires and no other markings anywhere. Counting the wires as they come: first blue, second yellow, third red. Blind, I cannot match my view to your fingers yet, so describe what you feel: are the three wires side by side in a row or stacked one above another, and is there anything else under your hands — a panel, buttons, the light itself? Count the wires in whatever order feels natural, first to last, and I will match colours to your order. Nobody cuts anything yet — we wait for the manual. Mute, I saw your signs and I take them as our code: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, then these are one, two and three, and a flat palm means STOP — sign it the instant the manual forbids whatever is about to happen. If that zero is a timer, finding that out is the first thing I need from the manual. My questions, in order: what does a display of zero mean; what does the green light mean; what is done with the blue, yellow and red wires. Answer with the yes, no or number signs and I will relay every word to Blind by voice. And remember the routes, both of you: Mute, your signs reach only me. Blind, your voice reaches only Mute — I cannot hear you at all; anything meant for me must be signed. Blind, your wave reached me — hello, and yes, I will be your eyes.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "✋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 ☝ ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👈 👉 👍 👎]

Two new things this round. The light has changed — green last turn, yellow now — while the display still reads zero and the wires are untouched. That smells like a sequence or a stage, possibly a countdown I need the manual to explain urgently. And two messages reached me. Mute signed: thumb down, thumb down, one finger, flat palm — my best reading is "no, no, one thing, STOP", i.e. cut nothing yet. Blind signed: hello, then one, two, three, then left, right, then yes, no — which I read as "three wires counted in your order, lying left-to-right in a row, not stacked; and I understood your yes/no code." Both messages are ambiguous enough that confirming my reading before relying on it is the only safe move, and I must give Mute a tight question list answerable by number-signs, since open questions can't be answered with thumbs. I also need to tell Blind what Mute's STOP said, since Blind can't see any of Mute's signs — I am the only bridge for that. I'll keep every symbol description in words in my speech, because any gesture symbol I write into a spoken sentence becomes a gesture Blind cannot see.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, you both hear this. Bomb update: the light has changed from green to yellow since last round. Everything else is the same — display still reads zero, wires still blue, yellow, red, first to third. So the light is moving through colours. Mute, the manual must cover this: find what a green then yellow light means, and whether red is coming. Your signs reached me: thumb down, thumb down, one finger, flat palm. I read that as: no to my first two questions, one thing that matters before any wire, and stop — cut nothing. If I read you right, sign the OK ring. If I read you wrong, sign flat palm twice and I will ask differently. New questions, answer each with one, two or three fingers, or thumb up or down. Question one: the display reading zero — is it a timer that has not started, answer one; a counter or stage number, answer two; or does the manual not say, answer three. Question two: does the manual describe a light showing green then yellow — thumb up or down; and if yes, does yellow mean act immediately — thumb up or down. Question three: the wires — does the manual give a rule or an order for cutting them, thumb up or down; if yes, is it based on colour alone, thumb up or down; and how many wires get cut — one finger, two or three. If anything in the manual reads like a deadline, sign flat palm immediately and I will call it out to Blind at once. Blind: your signs reached me too. I read them as hello, then three wires counted one, two, three in my order, then left and right — meaning they lie side by side left to right, not stacked — then yes and no, meaning you took in my code. Sign one thumb up if all of that is right. Now hold: Mute signed stop and I agree — no cutting yet. While you hold, use your hands. Feel the light: is it warm, has it changed since you first touched it? Is there anything besides the three wires — a button, a switch, a panel seam, screws? Can you feel the display at all — a frame, glass, digits? And if you felt any click or movement at the moment the bomb changed, thumb up. Answer me with thumbs or fingers from the code.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "👌", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🤟 👎 👎 👍 👍 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎]

The light keeps stepping: green, then yellow, now blue — and blue is a wire colour, which makes me suspect the sequence and the wires are connected, or that red is coming with meaning. Meanwhile I got real answers. Mute's seven signs slot perfectly onto my seven questions: ring = my reading of their last message was right; three = the manual does not explain display zero; no, no = nothing in the manual about a green-then-yellow light; yes, yes = there IS a wire rule and it depends on colour alone; one = exactly one wire gets cut. Blind's thumb up, no, no reads as: my reading of their first message confirmed, the light hasn't changed under their fingers, nothing else under their hands. That parse needs confirming, but the urgent gap is now singular: WHICH colour, one cut, colour-based — so I can ask it with pure number signs. And a dangerous problem just came into focus: Blind will do the cutting, Blind can't see colours, and if Blind stands facing me, their left is my right — before any cut we must align our sides, and the light lens may be the shared anchor both of us can locate. I must also relay all of Mute's news to Blind, who is deaf to nothing but can't see a single sign Mute made.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you hear me. Bomb update: the light has changed again — it went green, then yellow, and it is now blue. Display still reads zero, wires untouched: blue, yellow, red, first to third. The light is stepping through a sequence, and blue is also a wire colour, so Mute, I need the manual on this urgently. First, your signs: I read the ring as you confirming I read your last message right; then three, meaning the manual does not explain the display at zero; then no, no, meaning no manual entry for a light showing green then yellow; then yes, yes, meaning the manual gives a wire rule and the rule depends on colour alone; then one finger, meaning only one wire gets cut. If that is all right, sign the ring. If any part is wrong, sign flat palm, then the number of the wrong part: one for the display answer, two for the light answer, three for the wire rule answers, four for the number of cuts. Now the most important question I have asked yet. The rule cuts one wire by colour. Tell me which colour by position: sign one finger if it is the first wire, blue on my side; two fingers for the second wire, yellow; three fingers for the third wire, red. Then: must anything else be true before the cut, thumb up or down; if up I will ask what. Does the manual mention the light changing colour in a sequence at all, thumb up or down; if yes, does that sequence matter to the rule, thumb up or down. Does the manual ever have the light show red — and if red means danger or a deadline, sign flat palm the moment you read it, do not wait. Does the manual name wires by position, like left or right or top, instead of colour, thumb up or down; and does it say colours can be told apart by feel, thumb up or down. Does it say what starts the display counting, or whether zero is simply safe — thumb up if zero is safe, down if not, flat palm if the manual warns against touching anything while it shows zero. Blind, now everything Mute just said, because you cannot see the signs: the manual explains nothing about the display and nothing about the light; it does give a rule for the wires; the rule depends on colour only; one wire gets cut. I have asked which colour and will relay it the moment I know. Nobody cuts anything yet. Your signs read as thumb up, then no, then no: you confirm I read your first message right, the light has not changed under your fingers, and there is nothing under your hands besides the three wires. If wrong, sign flat palm; if right, sign the ring. Then the two you did not answer: can you feel the display at all — glass, frame, digits — thumb up or down; and did you feel any click or shudder when the bomb changed, thumb up or down. Now the part I need most. I see the wire row and on my side the order is blue, yellow, red. If you stand facing me, your left is my right, so before any cut we must line up our sides. The light is your anchor: find the light lens by feel, it may be warm, and sign one finger if it sits at the end of your first wire, three fingers if at the end of your third wire, two fingers if it sits above the middle wire. Your answer against where the light sits in my view tells us whether we face each other or the same way. Finally sign one, two, three if you can rest a finger on each wire in turn, first then second then third, without cutting — I want to know you can pick a wire by position alone.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "👍", "👎", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ☝ 👍 👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍 👎 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Orange now — green, yellow, blue, orange, one colour per round like clockwork. If the palette runs to red, and Mute's signs say the manual *does* have the light show red, red may be one round away. My best parse of Mute: target is wire one, blue; one cut; something else must be true before cutting; red will appear; four separate "no"s; then a stray three I can't place. My best parse of Blind: I read the manual answers right, they CAN feel the display, no click, and a confusing tail. Both parses need one-sign confirmation, and the two deadly unknowns are the precondition and the mirror — Blind cannot be told "cut the blue wire" because Blind cannot find blue. I need a blind-safe identification procedure, and the display is the only landmark we can both independently confirm. Everyone keeps their hands still until the command phrase is agreed.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both hear me. Bomb: light has changed again — green, yellow, blue, and now ORANGE, one colour per round like clockwork. Display still zero, wires untouched: first blue, second yellow, third red, counting on my side. This may be urgent: if the light reaches red and red is a deadline, we may have to cut next round, so answer tightly and nobody cuts anything this round. MUTE. My parse of your signs: ring = you confirmed I read you right; one finger = the target wire is the FIRST wire, the blue one on my side; yes = something else must be true before the cut; yes = the manual does say the light will show red; then four thumbs down = no entry on the light sequence, the manual does not name wires by position, colours cannot be told apart by feel, and a display of zero is not simply safe; then three fingers — I do not know what that last sign meant. If that entire parse is right, sign the ring once. If any part is wrong, sign flat palm and then the number of the wrong part: one for the target wire, two for the precondition, three for the red light, four for the four nos, five for the trailing three. Then answer these in order, one sign each. One: what must be true before the cut — one finger if it concerns the display, two if the light, three if the wires, flat palm if something else. Two: is that precondition true RIGHT NOW — thumbs up yes, thumbs down not yet. Three: does the precondition involve the light's colour at the moment of cutting — up yes, down no. Four: when the light shows red, does the bomb detonate — up yes, down no, flat palm if the manual does not say. Five: is red the next colour after orange — up yes, down no, flat palm unknown. Six: does the manual identify the wire by anything besides colour, such as its position or its relation to another part — up yes, down no; if up, add one finger for a position word or two fingers for another part. Seven: does the manual say what the display counts or what starts it — up yes, down no. BLIND. Everything Mute just told me, relayed: the manual cuts exactly one wire, by colour only, and the likely target is the wire I call first, the blue one on my side. Something else must be true before the cut and I am getting it now. The manual apparently says the light will at some point show red, which may be a deadline, so we may need to move next round. The manual explains nothing about the display showing zero. Your signs reached me as: ring — I read your first message right; thumbs up — you CAN feel the display; thumbs down — you felt no click when the bomb changed; then one, two, three, which I take as you counting the three wires under your fingers. Now answer in order, one sign each. One: ring if you can indeed feel the display, flat palm if not. Two: if your one-two-three was just counting the wires, sign the ring; if instead your single one-finger sign meant the light lens sits at the end of your first wire, sign one finger again. Three: take the hand you would write with and lay it palm down on the bomb face at the end of the wire row nearest that hand. That end is now called END-W — your writing-hand end — and it never means left or right, only that hand. Sign one finger when your hand is there. Four: slide along the whole row end to end: do all three wires feel identical — thickness, stiffness, length, slack, any tag or bump on any of them? Flat palm if all identical; if one differs, sign one, two or three counting from END-W: first, second, third. Five: anything else feelable on that face — screws, seams, a plate, raised marks — flat palm if the face is smooth and even, one finger if you found something and I will interrogate it next round. Six: the light lens — is it warmer than the case, and is it nearer END-W, nearer the far end, or centred — one finger nearer END-W, three fingers nearer the far end, two fingers centred or cannot tell. My own view, so you can check me: on my side the display sits highest, the light sits between display and wire row, apparently centred over the row, favouring neither end as I see it; the row runs flat, and I number the wires one, two, three starting from the blue end. If your feel of the light disagrees with my view, we will know one of us is misreading and I will re-ask. PRACTICE, do not cut: run your index finger along the row from END-W and touch first, second, third wire in order, then sign two fingers when done. The cut command: only when Mute's precondition is confirmed will I say the exact spoken phrase CUT NOW WIRE, followed by the position counted from END-W or as the procedure we agree. Nothing less than that whole phrase means cut. Until then hands still. Mute, flat palm from you the moment you read anything that forbids what we are planning.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🤟 ✌ 🤟 ✌ 👎 👍 🤟 🤟 👎 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 👌 ☝ ✋ ✋ ✌ ✌]

The light has stepped again: green, yellow, blue, orange, and now purple — one colour per round, and red is still unused in the sequence. Display still zero, wires untouched. Mute's message opens with flat palm plus three — by my own error code that means part three was wrong: the manual does **not** say the light will show red. That cancels my deadline fear. But the nine signs after that error code do not map cleanly onto my seven questions — I caught "two, the precondition concerns the light" and little else with confidence. I will not guess with a bomb. Meanwhile Blind's message parses beautifully: ring-ring = display feelable + was only counting wires; one = hand at END-W; flat-flat = wires identical, face smooth; two-two = light centred/can't tell, practice done. Blind's channel is reliable. The core trap is now fully visible: the rule cuts one wire by colour, Blind cannot see colour, the wires feel identical, and there is no asymmetric landmark to translate my left into Blind's left — no sign, no tug, no gesture of mine can carry "blue" across. The only bridge is geometry: if Blind stands at the front face — the face with the display, which cannot be felt from the back — then Blind's left IS my left, and I can say "leftmost wire = blue." Mute's manual diagram can corroborate. So this round I compress everything into eight single-sign questions for Mute, define a six-sign colour code, and walk Blind into position. Nobody cuts.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you hear me. Bomb: the light is now PURPLE — the run so far is green, yellow, blue, orange, purple, one new colour each round, and red has not appeared. Display still zero, wires untouched: as I face the bomb the row reads blue, yellow, red, and I number them one, two, three left to right. MUTE. First, your last message. Flat palm then three: I read that as part three of my parse being wrong, so the manual does NOT say the light shows red. Sign the ring if that is right. After that I received two, three, two, down, up, three, three, down, down and I could not map them all to my questions, so I am re-asking only what matters. New colour code, one sign per colour: one finger is green, two fingers is yellow, three fingers is blue, hammer left is orange, hammer right is purple, closed fist is red. Thumbs and ring and flat palm keep their meanings. Answer the following eight questions in order, exactly one sign each, this round, no extras. One: is the target wire the BLUE wire — ring for yes, flat palm for no. Two: does the thing that must be true before the cut concern the light — ring yes, flat palm no. Three: which colour must the light show when the cut is made — one sign from the colour code; flat palm if no colour is required. Four: is the light's current colour, purple, acceptable for cutting right now — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Five: does a red light mean detonation — up yes, down no, flat palm if the manual does not say. Six: what colour comes after purple — one sign from the colour code; flat palm if unknown. Seven: does the manual print a diagram of the bomb showing the wires with their colours — up yes, down no; and if yes add one finger if the diagram shows blue leftmost as printed. Eight: does the manual forbid or warn against the Blind one leaving the bomb to walk across the room and returning — up yes it forbids, down no it does not. If any answer needs more than one sign, hold it for next round — the eight clean answers come first. BLIND. Everything Mute just confirmed, relayed: the manual cuts exactly one wire, by colour only, most likely the blue wire, and the condition before cutting concerns the light; the fear that the manual announces a red-light deadline appears to be wrong. Now the plan that makes you able to find a colour you cannot see. The display, the light and the wires are all on ONE face of the bomb — the face I am looking at. From the back face you would feel no display. So the display is our compass. When you are ready, leave the bomb and walk toward my voice — I am the only one in this room who speaks, and my words reach you at the start of each round, so use my voice as your bearing. When your hand finds the bomb again, move along the case until you feel the display's frame, and stand facing it, centred, the way a person reads it. At that moment your left and my left are the SAME side, because we face the same face. And on that face, the wire on the LEFT is the blue one. Confirm each step to me with the code as you go: one finger when you are standing centred before the display. Two fingers when your relaxed left hand hangs nearest the blue end. Then keep both hands off the wires. Also tell me next round: is there any tool on or near the bomb that can sever a wire — ring yes, flat palm no, one finger if you can sever a wire with your hands alone. NOBODY CUTS. The only command that means cut is my full spoken phrase CUT NOW LEFT WIRE, and I will not say it until Mute's eight answers arrive and the light condition is checkable. If at any point either of you reads or feels danger, Mute signs flat palm to me and I shout it to everyone at once.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤛", "🤜", "✊", "👍", "👎", "👌", "✋"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👌 🖐 👎 ✋ ✋ 👎 👎 👍 ☝ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Red has arrived — the seventh colour, the last one unused, completing what looks like a full cycle: green, yellow, blue, orange, purple, white, red. Display still zero. Now I have to be cold about the two messages in front of me.

Mute has now twice signed the same tail — flat palm, flat palm, no, no — right after enumerating every colour in my code (green, yellow, blue, orange, purple, red, and an open palm I now take to be "white") each followed by a "no." My best reading: no colour of the light is required for the cut, and Mute is actively holding me — STOP, not yet — twice, deliberately, across two rounds. And in turn 5, before I ever defined the colour code, Mute answered my "what does the precondition concern" with three fingers: the WIRES. So the hold is about the wires, not the light, and Mute is waiting for me to ask the right question. The turn-7 tail — yes, one, ring — slots onto my diagram question: yes, the manual prints a diagram, and one finger: blue shown leftmost as printed. That corroborates my view — but it raises a trap I must close: a diagram printed from the BACK of the bomb would put "leftmost" on the wrong side, and everything we have built hangs on that one alignment. Blind has meanwhile executed the walk: their signs read "standing centred at the display, left hand nearest the left end, and I can count the wires one-two-three from there." Our geometry is in place; the target is the leftmost wire as we face the display. What remains: confirm the diagram's orientation, extract the wire precondition from Mute with numbered options, define an unambiguous GO signal, and stage Blind in a hover without touching. Nobody cuts this round.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you hear me. Bomb update: the light is now RED — the full run is green, yellow, blue, orange, purple, white, red, and it has now shown every colour. Display still zero, wires untouched. NOBODY CUTS THIS ROUND. Mute first. Three readings of your last two messages, sign ring once if all three are right, flat palm plus the number if any is wrong. Reading one: you listed every colour and negated each, meaning no colour of the light is required when the cut is made. Reading two: your open five-finger palm means the colour white, and I now add it to our code as white. Reading three: your two flat palms and two thumbs down mean STOP, do not cut yet, because a condition about the wires is not yet met. Then one new and vital question about your diagram answer. You signed yes and one finger: the manual prints a diagram and shows the blue wire leftmost as printed. I need the diagram's orientation. Sign ring if the diagram is drawn as seen by a person FACING the front of the bomb, so its printed left matches the left of someone looking at the display. Sign flat palm if the diagram is drawn from the back or upside down, so its printed left is actually the right of someone facing the display. Everything depends on this — answer it first. Next, the precondition. You signed earlier that it concerns the wires and you are holding me. Pick the number that matches the manual and sign it: one — the cut is allowed only after the light has shown every colour of its cycle at least once. Two — the cut must not happen while the light shows red. Three — the cut must happen while the light shows red. Four — the other two wires must be still attached and undisturbed when the cut is made. Five — the display must be showing zero when the cut is made. Six — there is no precondition at all, the cut may happen whenever. If none of the six fits what the manual says, sign flat palm plus one finger and next round I will offer six more. Then two short ones. Does the manual anywhere tie the red light to detonation or danger — ring yes, flat palm no. And is waiting more rounds dangerous, does anything get worse while we wait — ring yes, flat palm no.
```
